ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In a certain medium, there are two wave sources at positions $S_1$ and $S_2$, separated by a distance of 3m, oscillating harmonically in the direction perpendicular to the plane of the paper. Their periods are $T_1$=0.8s and $T_2$=0.2s, and their amplitudes are $A_1$=3cm and $A_2$=1cm, respectively. The speed of the harmonic waves formed in this medium is v=5m/s. At position S, there is a particle located 4m away from $S_1$, and $SS_1$ is perpendicular to $S_1S_2$. At time t=0, both wave sources simultaneously begin to oscillate outward perpendicular to the plane of the paper.

1. What is the time difference for the vibration to reach point S at the moment $t=0$?
2. At $t = 6 \, \text{s}$, what is the displacement magnitude of the particle at point $S$ from its equilibrium position?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, point S is located directly above point S1, and S2 is located to the right of S1; SS1 is a vertical dashed line segment, S1S2 is a horizontal dashed line segment, and SS2 is an oblique dashed line segment, therefore S, S1, and S2 form a right triangle with S1 as the right-angle vertex. Reasoning: It is known that SS1 = 4 m and S1S2 = 3 m, so by the Pythagorean theorem, SS2 = sqrt(4^2 + 3^2) = 5 m. The wave speed v = 5 m/s, therefore the propagation time from S1 to S is t1 = 4/5 = 0.8 s, and the propagation time from S2 to S is t2 = 5/5 = 1.0 s. The time difference of arrival at S is 1.0 - 0.8 = 0.2 s. At t = 6 s, use the delay time to calculate the displacement of the two waves at S. The two wave sources start vibrating outward from the equilibrium position, so take the sine form: y1 = A1 sin[2π(6 - 0.8)/T1], y2 = A2 sin[2π(6 - 1.0)/T2]. Substitute T1 = 0.8 s and T2 = 0.2 s: for S1, (6 - 0.8)/0.8 = 6.5 cycles, sin(13π) = 0; for S2, (6 - 1.0)/0.2 = 25 cycles, sin(50π) = 0. Therefore the resultant displacement is 0, and the displacement magnitude is 0 cm.
